operational-example.copy: Use Tag for compact metadata that labels type, platform, category, support level, or risk without implying selection, removal, or navigation.

scenario.title: Component metadata
rationale: Tags describe metadata without becoming a control.
Tone supports scan value while the visible label carries meaning.
Interactive tags are reserved for metadata that actually filters or navigates.

items.rule: Owns compact label shape, surface, border, density, and optional focus.
Names the metadata value in concise language.
Optional semantic treatment supports status or risk without replacing text.
Supports recognition only when it clarifies the label.
Keeps static tags unfocusable and applies button or link semantics only when behavior exists.

items: Render as text when Tag only describes metadata.
Use button or link semantics only when the tag filters or navigates.
Keep the visible label as the accessible name.
Do not use color alone for semantic tone.
Do not expose selected or removable behavior; use Chip when metadata becomes a token or filter.

variants.copy: Tag variants describe metadata purpose: neutral labels, semantic status, platform labels, and clickable metadata when behavior is explicit.

states.copy: Tag states are intentionally limited. Static tags do not hover or press; interactive tags may expose hover, focus, pressed, and disabled.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines metadata meaning; state exists only when the tag is interactive. Static metadata keeps default state.

full-width.copy: Tag keeps intrinsic width. Parent layouts may wrap tags, but a single tag does not stretch or behave like a button group.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Responsive tag groups wrap near the object they describe and avoid crowding mobile headers with low-value metadata.

viewport-organization.copy: Show only metadata that helps the user scan or decide. Move dense classification into a catalog or filter pattern.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Show one or two high-value tags close to the object title.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Allow metadata rows to wrap without pushing primary actions away.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use tags for catalog metadata, support states, and classification near tables.

playground.copy: Use the playground to confirm label length, tone, icon, and whether the tag is static metadata or a real interactive affordance.

api-foundations.copy: Tag API exposes label, variant, tone, optional icon, state, and interactive behavior while Design System foundations own metadata hierarchy, tone, focus, and density.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Metadata purpose: metadata, status, platform, or link.

props.name: state
props.notes: Local display state for interactive tags.

props.name: interactive
props.notes: Renders the tag as an interactive button.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for compact metadata, categories, platform labels, and support states.
Use interactive only when the tag actually filters or navigates.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use Tag for counts; use Badge.
Do not use Tag for selected or removable filters; use Chip.
Do not use Tag to switch panels; use Tabs.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm whether the tag is static or interactive.
Check tone contrast and label clarity.
Verify dense groups do not replace a filter pattern.

mustTest: Interactive tags have button or link semantics
Tag groups wrap without layout overflow
rejectIf: Tag pretends to be selected or removable.
Tag replaces Badge, Chip, Tabs, or Button behavior.
Color is the only semantic signal.
Interactive tag has no destination or action.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Tag as metadata, not a control by default: agents can label objects when taxonomy is explicit, while humans confirm interaction, source of truth, and whether classification belongs in a pattern.
canDecide: Use Tag for metadata, category, platform, support level, or semantic status.
Keep Tag static when it only describes an object.
Use tone only when the metadata has explicit semantic meaning.
mustAsk: The tag should filter, navigate, or change state.
The taxonomy, support level, or metadata source is unclear.
The label might belong to Badge, Chip, Tabs, or Button instead.
rejectIf: Tag is used for selected or removable filters.
Tag is used as a standalone action.
Tag color carries meaning without visible text.
miel.handoff: I am using Tag as metadata. I need confirmation on taxonomy, source of truth, and whether any tag is truly interactive.
